chunks: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Consider whom you converse with, for there is no one upon whom death descends except that his companions are presented to him before God — if they were good, then good; and if they were evil, then evil. And there is no one who dies except that I present myself to him at his death.'

key_terms.تَمَثَّلْتُ: I present myself/appear; first-person singular, spoken by Imam Ali (AS) asserting his spiritual presence at death
key_terms.تُحَادِثُونَ: Those you converse with, associate with; implies ongoing companionship and social relations
key_terms.خِيَاراً: The good/righteous ones; those of excellent moral character
key_terms.شِرَاراً: The evil/wicked ones; those of corrupt moral character
key_terms.مُثِّلَ: Is presented/depicted; the passive form implies divine agency in this presentation at death

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali narrate about companions and death in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) narrates a prophetic hadith in which the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) warns believers to be mindful of their companions and social circles. The hadith teaches two realities about death: first, that at the moment of death, a person sees an image of their companions presented before God, reflecting the moral quality of those companions back upon the dying person. Second, Imam Ali (AS) adds his own testimony that he personally appears to every dying person at the moment of their death. This dual teaching was addressed to early Muslim communities in Kufa who were grappling with questions of social loyalty and eschatological accountability.
